replace.grasp_plan:
Generate inspectable public RGB-D grasp candidates for one current target.
Use when: current grounding or segmentation identifies the intended object and you need parallel-jaw poses. Select the arm on dual-arm embodiments.
Effect: read-only; queries Contact-GraspNet using the selected source-camera RGB-D and compiles poses to the ARX X5 link6 controlled point; the embodiment card gives its fixed offset to the jaw contact centre. Top-down candidates from the target mask (jaw centre at a support-aware mid-height) join the learned ones. Optional synchronized views provide review evidence.
Returns: up to three candidates, complete world-frame pregrasp_pose and contact_pose, copyable bounded contact_approach targets, predicted opening, compiler checks and labeled review images. gripper_opening_m is the learned width prediction or, top-down, the mask width plus clearance, admitted up to the 80 mm nominal ceiling; aperture_calibration states that it is not measured pad clearance. Reachability is delegated to move_pose or grasp_execute; this call does not run a motion probe or return a plan_ref. Inspect every candidate panel and choose target identity and geometry independently of rank. After choosing a current candidate, use grasp_execute(candidate_id, rationale) when you accept its committed open/pregrasp/approach/close/lift/verify sequence without intermediate decisions. Choose manual move_pose plus set_gripper when you need a separate observation or decision before closing. Choose this path before moving: any world action stales the candidate, so call grasp_plan again before later using grasp_execute. Pose handoff: when manually commanding a returned world pose, set position_mode=absolute and orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion, then copy position_m and orientation_xyzw unchanged. Put these fields under targets.<selected_arm>. Choose interaction by the intended physical contact. Schema example only; replace the illustrative pose and arm with your selected current result:
{"tool":"move_pose","arguments":{"targets":{"right":{"position_mode":"absolute","position_m":[0.1,0.0,0.9],"orientation_mode":"absolute_quaternion","orientation_xyzw":[0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0],"interaction":"precision"}}}}
Does not: plan trajectories, certify reachability, move the robot, command a gripper, use object ground truth, certify retention or report task success. Backend rank is not a success probability. Missing optional review cameras do not invalidate usable primary input.
On error: obtain a better current view or select another target or candidate. Recompute after the target or observation changes. After a submitted motion fails, use its phase and measured residual to choose the next action. Retention evidence remains advisory. Prepared grasp selection: grasp_execute opens first and releases anything held, then uses the candidate pregrasp and contact poses and a 3 cm world-up probe. Select it only when opening and lifting are appropriate; otherwise use manual motion. Candidates are geometry proposals, not reachability certificates. For grasp_execute, the selected pregrasp receives one backend check before opening. Manual pose submissions use normal backend admission.
